errors.location: Theorem 2.1 and the displayed formula defining phi_C
errors.description: The stated residue formula does not descend to the quotient by Jac(S): a zero quotient class can have a nonzero residue image.
errors.evidence: For n=2, e=3 and G=x0^3+x1^3+x2^3, y*x0*G0 belongs to Jac(S) and has charge zero. However, d[x0*(x2 dx1-x1 dx2)/G]=Omega_x/G-x0*G0*Omega_x/G^2. The displayed formula therefore sends this zero class to -res(Omega_x/G)=-phi_C([1]), which is nonzero by the claimed isomorphism and Example 2.4.

errors.location: Theorem 2.3, equation (2.10), and its proof's final paragraph
errors.description: Matching one cup-product value cannot determine the conjugate class in a Hodge component of dimension greater than one. The formula's arbitrary choice of g can produce different purported conjugates of the same class.
errors.evidence: The theorem permits 'any polynomial' g with r_(f*g) nonzero, while the proof identifies conjugation using only R(y^i f,y^(n-1-i)h)=U_(k,gamma). For a smooth plane quartic, the manuscript's dimension formula gives mu=6 and |I0|=|I1|=3. The linear functional [g] -> r_(f*g) on the three-dimensional complementary component has a nonzero kernel. Replacing g by g+v for a nonzero kernel class preserves the denominator in (2.10) but changes the resulting class, so both choices cannot equal the unique conjugate.

errors.location: Section 2.4, definition U_(k,gamma)=diagonal(P_X P conjugate(P_X)^T), and its extension of Theorem 2.3
errors.description: For even-dimensional hypersurfaces, the cup product expressed in cycle periods uses the inverse intersection matrix. Using P itself gives the wrong normalization and invalidates the asserted extension.
errors.evidence: Section 2.4 states det(P)=+/-e and uses P_X P conjugate(P_X)^T. If a cohomology class has period column a on the cycle basis, its Poincare-dual cycle has coefficients P^(-1)a; thus its pairing with a class of periods b is a^T P^(-1)b. Since e>1, P cannot equal P^(-1): their determinant magnitudes are e and 1/e. The odd-dimensional symplectic normalization does not justify using P in this case.

errors.description: The proposed real cohomology contains imaginary multiples of conjugation-fixed nonzero classes, which are not real classes. The claimed spanning formula is therefore false.
errors.evidence: Equation (2.19) defines w=(U+conjugate(U))/2 under the theorem's claimed conjugation relation, so conjugate(w)=w. Corollary 2.7 nevertheless includes both R[w] and R[sqrt(-1)w]. Conjugation sends sqrt(-1)w to -sqrt(-1)w, so this vector is not fixed when w is nonzero. For n even, U and its conjugate lie in distinct Hodge components, ensuring w is nonzero. Example 2.8 repeats this same incorrect real spanning formula.
